answer: No. The only approve handler comes from the TRANSITIONS table, whose approve row has from = null, so the status guard is skipped and any order (O, A, R) can be set to A; nothing else enforces it (files read: srv/order-service.js, srv/order-service.cds, srv/admin-service.cds, db/schema.cds, package.json, app/services.cds, app/orders/annotations.cds). The repo's own test 'approve only in state S' expects 409 and would fail against this code.

findings.title: Orders.approve has no server-side status_code = S check
findings.statement: The UI hides approve unless status_code = 'S', but the generic transition handler registers approve with from = null, and the guard `if (from && order.status_code !== from)` is therefore skipped for approve; the handler goes straight to UPDATE status_code = 'A'. No other handler, DB constraint (status is a plain association with default 'O') or plugin is configured, so an Approver can approve an Open or already Rejected order by calling the action directly.
